# Answer: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed generator emits such cases.

## Strongest tested shortcut: launch only toward the center

The **centerward-only** rival launches along the green seed's axis only toward
the farther boundary (toward the center), then otherwise obeys the normal cyan
splitting rule. Ties launch toward increasing coordinates. This is a plausible
shortcut because every canonical seed touches an axial boundary: an outward
launch contributes nothing there. It fits all **6/6 labeled canonical records**,
which are **three unique pairs**, including the canonical query labels used for
review verification. I regard it as stronger than a contrived memorization rule
because it removes a meaningful part of the launch semantics.

Two additional rivals also fit 6/6: `axis_edge_only` activates rays only when
the seed touches an axial boundary, and `cluster_absorbs` makes a cyan cell
absorb a ray if it has an orthogonally adjacent cyan neighbor. They are declared
and checked separately. The other six final competitors are useful teaching
rivals but do not fit all canonical records.

## An exact input actually emitted by the final generator

Reproduce with version **4.1.1**:

```python
generate(seed=0, sample_index=0, difficulty="easy")
```

No overrides or edited cells are used. Input: **5 rows × 6 columns**.
Intended output: **5 rows × 6 columns**. Rival output: **5 rows × 6 columns**.

```json
{
  "input": [
    [7,7,7,8,8,7],
    [7,7,8,7,3,7],
    [7,7,8,7,3,7],
    [7,7,7,8,7,7],
    [7,7,7,7,7,7]
  ],
  "racket_output": [
    [7,7,7,8,8,7],
    [7,7,8,3,3,3],
    [7,7,8,3,3,3],
    [7,7,7,8,3,7],
    [7,7,7,7,3,7]
  ],
  "centerward_only_output": [
    [7,7,7,8,8,7],
    [7,7,8,7,3,7],
    [7,7,8,7,3,7],
    [7,7,7,8,3,7],
    [7,7,7,7,3,7]
  ]
}
```

At zero-based **(1,3), (1,5), (2,3), and (2,5)** the intended output is green
`3`, while the centerward-only rival leaves orange `7`. The upward beam meets
cyan at (0,4), splits horizontally from (1,4), and later turns again before the
other cyan cells. The downward-only shortcut misses those branches. The same
input refutes cluster absorption at those four cells and the edge-only rival
at six cells.

## Verification and emitted support

The input was replayed exactly from the final generator and passed `self_check`.
Its output was obtained independently with the public **`Catalog.apply`** API
using canonical Racket; it is sample 0 in batch 0 of
`checks/laser-probe-final.json`. The receipt records rule `610c94f513d9`, rule-text
SHA-256 `4a7c73d80dd544327867337a14299ee2306cf7deb8a949438a500b9c6694a9b2`,
and generator SHA-256
`aa9940392c76ce0e2006361be2bb1c4e874ea6bb0969d96106a62783941744af`.
This is reference execution, not a Python mirror supplying its own expected label.

`repo/generators/646eeb47599b/counterexamples/generator-shortcuts.json` retains
the input, full outputs for all three rivals, every differing coordinate, exact
generation call, canonical-fit counts and receipt hashes. The source patch adds
this file. `checks/build_question_witness.py` replays and checks its provenance.

**Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases.** The witness is an actual
default teaching draw and also the first pair of the final fixed-seed production
enumeration. Each successful unpinned teaching draw distinguishes all nine
declared rivals; one broad draw follows each pair of teaching draws. With three
demonstrations and one query at consecutive accepted indices, every query
rotation leaves a distinguishing teaching example. The final measured scope is
0/300 ambiguous production lessons and 0/1,200 ambiguous rotations, plus full
period-three enumeration at seed 0: 0/9 and 0/36 respectively. These finite
results do not certify undeclared hypotheses, arbitrary skips, pinned lessons,
or every possible random seed.
